The image presents two pie charts displaying data related to the structure of a Chinese linguistic phenomenon.

The larger chart on the left shows the distribution across three categories. The largest slice, colored yellow, represents the combination of a single-syllable adjective and a single-syllable noun, accounting for 229 cases or 69.39%. The second-largest slice, colored blue, represents the combination of a disyllabic adjective and a single-syllable noun, with 101 cases or 30.61%. No other slices are present in this chart. A legend at the bottom indicates that the colors correspond to the categories as follows: blue (1), yellow (2), and green (3), though green is not utilized in the larger chart.

The smaller chart on the right displays data across two slices. The orange slice, representing cases where the character "de" is only implied and not visible, accounts for 81.66%. The green slice, representing cases where "de" is explicitly present, accounts for 18.34%. 

No slices are visually emphasized through enlargement, offsetting, or bolding. The slices in both charts appear to be arranged in descending order of their percentages. Both charts include percentage labels within their respective slices.
